title: Cross-account snapshot and lifecycle Terraform module for storage with encryption-first defaults
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Goal: Deliver a single, composable Terraform module that codifies best-practice storage primitives for private/VPC deployments (EBS volumes, EFS filesystems, S3 buckets) with encryption-first defaults, snapshot lifecycle policies, cross-account snapshot sharing patterns for backups, and automated health checks.

Scope:
- Module(s) to provision EBS volumes with KMS encryption keys and snapshot lifecycle rules.
- EFS module that configures encryption at rest, lifecycle transition for infrequent access, and automated backups (via DataSync/backup lambda pattern).
- S3 module with enforced bucket encryption (customer-managed KMS by default), object lock support opt-in, lifecycle rules for snapshots/archives, and cross-account replication templates for DR.
- Cross-account snapshot operator: minimal IAM policy templates and S3 bucket/policy examples to allow controlled snapshot export/import between customer accounts and central backup account.
- Health check primitives: Lambda-backed checks (or CloudWatch synthetic alarms) to validate snapshot completion, encryption key accessibility, and lifecycle rule execution; module exposes SNS/CloudWatch alarms.
- Upgrade and migration path documentation and Terraform upgrade helpers for state moves and resource replacement minimization.

Non-goals: OS-level snapshot orchestration, application-consistent quiescing (we will document recommended hooks but not implement), or provider-agnostic storage abstractions (AWS-first for private deployments).

Design decisions and constraints:
- Encryption precedence: default to a customer-managed KMS key (CMK) per environment; fall back to AWS managed CMKs only when explicitly allowed via a flag. Document key rotation guidance and grant patterns for cross-account access using key grants.
- Immutable snapshots: provide optional retention and governance via S3 object lock for exported snapshots; module exposes an "immutability_policy" param.
- Least-privilege IAM: generate modular IAM policies for snapshot sharing and snapshot import that can be used by central backup roles. Include example Terraform data sources for creating the ARNs in cross-account scenarios.
- Lifecycle policies: provide sane defaults (30d to cold storage for snapshots/objects) but surface parameters for tuning by workload.
- Health checks: implement an optional Lambda that runs nightly and reports metrics to a CloudWatch namespace (redwood/storage-module). Offer alarm templates for latency/failure thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module deploys EBS/EFS/S3 resources with encryption enabled by default in an isolated VPC test account.
- Snapshot lifecycle rules are created and observed via CloudWatch events in staged environment.
- Cross-account snapshot sharing documented end-to-end; example terraform config successfully copies a snapshot to a central backup account in a test run.
- Health check Lambda runs nightly in staging and creates at least one synthetic alarm that fires on intentionally failing test snapshot.
- Upgrade guide written covering terraform v1.5 -> 1.6, provider changes, and recommended state migration steps.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module repository under infra/modules/storage-cross-account (module code, examples, README).
- CI pipeline (GitHub Actions) for fmt/validate/plan with a policy check for no plaintext KMS keys.
- Migration helper script for state renames and resource replacements.
- Confluence doc: "Storage TF module - design, upgrade path, runbook" with diagrams and customer-facing notes.

Links to artifacts: Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRA/pages/Storage-TF-Module (draft), GH example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3052 (WIP).
updates: 2025-02-12 - Maya Thompson: Created ticket and draft design. Added initial scope and acceptance criteria. Assigned to Diego for technical design.

2025-02-18 - Diego Alvarez: Completed first-pass module layout. Chose KMS CMK-per-env pattern. Posted design diff in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3052. Requested review from Security (Aisha Patel).

2025-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Security review notes: prefer key grants over cross-account IAM roles where possible; require explicit opt-in for AWS-managed keys. Marked security_review_required=true and added checklist.

2025-02-25 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented health-check lambda prototype and CloudWatch namespace. Found IAM escalation edge-case when granting decrypt to central backup account; proposed fix by using conditional grants in KMS. Opened subtask ENG-48211 for IAM policy templating.
2025-03-04 - Maya Thompson: Reviewed module examples. Requested clearer docs on upgrade path (state migration steps). Added due_date 2025-03-22 and increased estimate to 8 points.
acceptance_criteria: Module deploys with encryption-first defaults (CMK) without manual overrides needed
Cross-account snapshot copy demo completes in test account using sample terraform configuration
Automated health check produces CloudWatch metrics and an alarm in staging
Upgrade guide drafted and validated via a dry-run migration in staging
notes: Trade-offs considered: single monolithic module vs composition. We chose composition: base module for encryption + resource modules for EBS/EFS/S3 to reduce blast radius on upgrades.
Testing plan: use isolated test AWS account per CI job; run end-to-end snapshot lifecycle in a sandbox with synthetic data to validate retention and cross-account copy.
Follow-ups: ENG-48211 (IAM policy templates), ENG-48212 (e2e CI playbook for module).
